theorem_title: Lemma 2.6 — simultaneous preliminary expansion with little-o failure
formal_statement:
namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

open Filter
/-- Lemma 2.6. Multiplication by n^(1/ε) retains its little-o assertion. -/
theorem preliminary_expansion (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / 2)
    (g : ∀ n, Geometry (dimension ε) n) :
    Tendsto (fun n =>
      uniformProb (fun s : Forms (g n).F (dimension ε) (arity ε) =>
        ¬ PreliminaryGood ε n (g n) s) * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / ε))
      atTop (nhds 0) := by sorry

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
natural_language_statement:
Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and the construction parameters. Let $f(n)$ be the probability, over the independent per-level-set linear forms, that at least one row set $S$ with $|S|\le n^{1-\varepsilon}$ violates the preliminary expansion bound. Then
$$f(n)n^{1/\varepsilon}\longrightarrow0,\qquad |\Gamma_A(S)|\ge(k-d+1)|S|\ \text{outside that failure event}.$$
The event quantifies simultaneously over all such row sets, including the empty set. It uses the specified fixed layer forms and all independent random coefficient vectors.

This gives the complete little-o expansion estimate before hashing. It is uniform in the choice of compatible field and public enumeration.

Differences from the source:
- encoding: failure probability o(n^{−1/ε}) → failure probability multiplied by the real power n^{1/ε} converges to zero; reason: this is the exact little-o assertion; n tends to infinity and is eventually positive
- encoding: simultaneous expansion for all small row sets → the complement of PreliminaryGood under the uniform law on all coefficient vectors; reason: the event and the complete independent sampling law are unchanged
